motivation_or_inadequacy: Training-law hidden-rate residuals cannot certify a deployed controller without coverage; an explicit three-state family disproves that transfer.
object_definition: Random-stop action/history occupation measure of a frozen controller, paired with an actively acquired squared hidden aggregate-rate error against a frozen visible-history hazard predictor.
primitive_operations: Independent reset and replay of the frozen unprobed policy
Independent random occupation stop with preserved physical state
Nonstationary response completion of the aggregate-rate second moment
Chebyshev time-jet estimation on a fixed bounded interval
consistency_conditions: No probe effect before the stop; every raw mean starts from the same unprobed prefix distribution
Actual product setting is distinct from sequential pulses
Within-label neutrality or actual all-microscopic-event access
All target, primitive and product exit rates bounded by supplied R
Frozen controller and predictor; independent final validation after adaptive training
relations_to_existing_mathematics: Strong lumpability and Markov path coupling
Positive Gram synthesis from N718 original proof
Classical birthday lower bound for uniformity testing
substantive_consequences: Sound whole-visible-path TV certificate without hidden density domination, hidden-state count or rare-label inversion
Simultaneous error control for every bounded path functional of one tested feedback policy
Promise separation: four-label prefix-tree family requires exponential passive restarts in horizon while bounded geometric probes permit polynomial active certification

theorem_candidates.statement: TV(P,Phat)<=min(1,T sqrt((k-1)D)) for D=(1/T)E integral ||Q^(J_t)E(X_t,:)-vhat(t,H_t)||_2^2 dt.
D=G-2Bpred+Cpred, with G acquired by nonstationary product-response completion and Bpred a frozen-prediction first-time derivative.

Fixed-interval Chebyshev acquisition has first, second and mixed derivative weight l1 norms 2n^2, (4/3)n^2(n^2-1), and 4n^4; factorial bias and bounded observations give finite confidence with n=O(log(1/theta)).
